label: Confirmed Cases (2026 DRC + Uganda + France)
source: WHO Regional Office for Africa Situation Report #15 / UN News / Africanews — 23–25 August 2026
contestNote: WHO Sitrep #15 (data as of 23 August): 5,584 confirmed cases and 2,680 deaths across 57 health zones in 6 provinces, up 563 cases and 302 deaths from the 18 August report. Africanews (25 August) separately cited 5,514 cases and 2,690+ deaths, a discrepancy typical of the lag between weekly WHO sitreps and daily press figures. Uganda's outbreak was declared officially over 28 July 2026 (20 confirmed, 18 recoveries, 2 deaths). France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. Africa CDC officials warned 22 August that the true case count may be 2-3x higher (10,000-15,000) given official detection captures an estimated 30-40% of infections, and that transmission may have begun as early as February 2026, months before the 15 May declaration.

This is now the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC history and the second-largest ever recorded worldwide, behind only the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic (28,616 cases). WHO's 100-day assessment (24 August) recorded an average of nearly 90 new confirmed cases per day over the outbreak's first three months.

The toll surpassed the 2,299 deaths of DRC's 2018-2020 Kivu outbreak, making this the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history. label: Case Fatality Rate (2026 BDBV)
value: ~48.0% (DRC, crude, as of 23 Aug); ~70% in North Kivu
source: WHO Regional Office for Africa Situation Report #15 / UN News 100-day assessment — 23–24 August 2026
contestNote: Crude national CFR calculated from reported confirmed cases/deaths; DRC's overall CFR has climbed from roughly 20% in early June to ~48.0% by 23 August as the outbreak has spread into less-accessible, less-resourced health zones. Province-level variation is stark: North Kivu's CFR has reached roughly 70%, well above the national average, which responders and outside experts attribute to weaker treatment access rather than a change in virus behavior. Africa CDC warned 22 August that if the official case count captures only 30-40% of true infections, the true CFR could be substantially lower than the crude reported figure. BDBV historically 25–47% CFR; this outbreak's crude national CFR now sits at or above the top of the historical range.

label: BDBV Vaccine Status — 70,000 Ervebo Doses Allocated, Phase 3 Trial Targeting Mid-September
value: 70,000 Ervebo doses released to DRC (20,000 for Phase 3 trial + 50,000 for frontline/health workers); human trial could begin by mid-September
source: WHO / Africa CDC / ICG / STAT News / Healio — 12–21 August 2026
contestNote: 20 August: WHO and Africa CDC announced the ICG approved immediate release of 70,000 Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) doses to DRC — 20,000 for a Phase 3 clinical trial testing cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus, 50,000 for frontline and health workers. WHO cautioned 'it is not known whether Ervebo may be protective against the Bundibugyo virus in humans,' though early lab/animal data suggest possible partial protection. As of 21 August the human trial had not yet launched; WHO/DRC talks target a start by mid-September pending shipment, DRC regulatory/ethics approval and team training. Animal data: 3/4 vaccinated primates survived BDBV challenge vs 1/4 controls; a ferret study showed 100% protection with a research-grade formulation vs 0% in controls. Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV (UK trial since 24 July) and Moderna's mRNA candidate (Canada Phase 1, early August) remain in earlier-stage animal/human safety trials and may be added later.
delta: 70,000-dose allocation approved 20 August; mid-September target date for Phase 3 launch reported 21 August
deltaNote: The 28 May WHO expert panel ruling barred Ervebo use outside research settings; the 7 August TAG-CVP recommendation, 12 August trial talks, 20 August dose allocation, and a mid-September target launch are successive steps toward a structured clinical trial pathway rather than a resumption of off-label ring vaccination. Since the ICG mechanism's 2021 establishment, over 56,000 Ervebo doses have been allocated for DRC outbreaks combined, plus 167,000 doses in preventive campaigns across five countries.

label: DRC Provinces + Countries Affected
value: 6 DRC provinces (57 health zones) + Uganda (outbreak closed) + France (recovered) + Germany (treated)
source: WHO Regional Office for Africa Situation Report #15 — 23 August 2026
delta: 57 of 151 health zones affected as of 23 August, up from ~54-55 on 20 August
deltaNote: Ituri Province remains the epicenter, accounting for ~85% of cases and 79% of deaths per WHO's 100-day review. North Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, South Kivu and Bas-Uélé round out the six affected provinces. Two newly affected health zones were confirmed in the 23 August WHO sitrep: Viadana (Bas-Uélé) and Mutwanga (North Kivu). UN News described the affected area as larger than France. Bas-Uélé borders Central African Republic conflict-displacement corridors and has poor road/communications access. Uganda's outbreak (Kampala + Wakiso) was declared over 28 July. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains largely inaccessible to response teams. WHO's second IHR Emergency Committee meeting (24 August) maintained PHEIC status and expanded 'high risk' guidance to nine bordering states including Burundi and the Central African Republic.

label: Contact Tracing Coverage (DRC)
value: ~83.4% of identified contacts under active follow-up
source: WHO Regional Office for Africa Situation Report #15 — 23 August 2026
delta: Coverage recovered slightly to ~83.4% (23 August) from ~82.9% (20 August), still below the 84% recorded 18 August and well under the 90%+ containment threshold
deltaNote: WHO reported active follow-up at 83.4% of identified contacts as of the 23 August sitrep, up marginally from 82.9% on 20 August but below the 84% figure WHO's 100-day review (24 August) cited for 18 August — small week-to-week fluctuations reflect the strain of tracing a still-accelerating caseload. WHO's 100-day assessment noted tracing coverage had climbed dramatically from just 9% in the outbreak's first week. Mercy Corps separately warned 60-70% of new cases are recorded outside monitored contacts, with confirmed cases now just 35km from the South Sudan border; a Lancet Infectious Diseases modelling study put the probability of Ebola spillover into South Sudan at roughly 69-70%. Uganda's contact-tracing program is closed following the 28 July outbreak-end declaration. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains a contact-tracing dead zone.
